effects: The signer sends exactly `assets` cbBTC to the vault, using the signer's cbBTC allowance to the vault.
The vault mints gtcbBTCc shares to `receiver`; the share amount comes from the vault's share price in storage, and the call sets no minimum.
The vault supplies the cbBTC to Morpho Blue markets and accrues the curator fee as new shares, which sets the share price the signer gets.
formats.shown: Intent 'Deposit', with the cbBTC amount deposited, the share ticker gtcbBTCc, and the share recipient.

findings.title: deposit does not show how many shares the receiver gets, because the vault computes it from storage.
findings.evidence: MetaMorpho.deposit: `shares = _convertToSharesWithTotals(assets, totalSupply(), newTotalAssets, Math.Rounding.Floor);` No calldata parameter holds the share amount. Case 0: the signer receives 49130934839788 gtcbBTCc, and the screen shows only the ticker 'gtcbBTCc'.

findings.title: deposit intent 'Deposit' names neither the asset nor the vault shares received in return.
findings.evidence: descriptor deposit format: `"intent": "Deposit"`. The asset and the shares appear only in the fields 'Deposit asset' and 'Share ticker'.
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Deposit cbBTC for gtcbBTCc shares" and add an interpolatedIntent "Deposit {assets} for gtcbBTCc shares to {receiver}".

cases.notes: The cbBTC out (4948 sats = 0.00004948 cbBTC) matches the screen. The shares in go to the signer, and the screen shows their ticker and recipient but not the amount (49130934839788 wei); the code sets no bound.

effects: The signer sends cbBTC to the vault. The vault computes the amount from `shares` and its share price in storage, rounding up, and the call sets no maximum. The only limit is the signer's allowance.
The vault mints exactly `shares` gtcbBTCc to `receiver`.
The vault supplies the cbBTC to Morpho Blue and accrues the curator fee shares first.
formats.shown: Intent 'Mint', a 'Deposit asset' field that shows only the ticker cbBTC, the share amount minted, and the share recipient.

findings.title: mint does not show how much cbBTC leaves the signer, because the vault computes it from storage.
findings.evidence: MetaMorpho.mint: `assets = _convertToAssetsWithTotals(shares, totalSupply(), newTotalAssets, Math.Rounding.Ceil);` and ERC4626._deposit: `SafeERC20.safeTransferFrom(_asset, caller, address(this), assets);`. Case 1: the signer sends 101 sats of cbBTC, and the screen shows 'Deposit asset: cbBTC' with no amount.

findings.title: mint label 'Deposit asset' holds only a ticker, so it reads as if an amount is missing or zero.
findings.evidence: descriptor mint format: `{"label": "Deposit asset", "format": "raw", "value": "$.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker"}`. The deposit format uses the same label for an amount. Case 1 screen: 'Deposit asset: cbBTC'.
findings.fix: Change the label to "Pay with (amount set by vault price)" or "Asset paid", and the intent to "Mint gtcbBTCc shares with cbBTC".

cases.notes: The only signer effect is 101 sats of cbBTC out. The screen names cbBTC but not the amount. The 999000000000 shares go to 0xdead (signer null), and the screen states that correctly.

formats.key: withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address owner)
effects: The vault burns gtcbBTCc shares from `owner`. It computes the amount from `assets` and the share price, rounding up, and the call sets no maximum.
When the caller is not `owner`, the call spends the owner's share allowance to the caller by that share amount.
The vault withdraws `assets` cbBTC from Morpho Blue and sends exactly `assets` cbBTC to `receiver`.
formats.shown: Intent 'Withdraw', the exact cbBTC amount withdrawn, the recipient and the owner of the shares.

findings.title: withdraw does not show how many shares the vault burns from the owner, because the vault computes it.
findings.evidence: MetaMorpho.withdraw: `shares = _convertToSharesWithTotals(assets, totalSupply(), newTotalAssets, Math.Rounding.Ceil);` and ERC4626._withdraw: `_burn(owner, shares);`. Case 2: the signer loses 1290996558190803 gtcbBTCc, and the screen shows no share amount.

findings.title: withdraw intent 'Withdraw' does not say that vault shares are burned to pay for the cbBTC.
findings.evidence: descriptor withdraw format: `"intent": "Withdraw"`. No field names gtcbBTCc as the asset that leaves the owner.
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Withdraw cbBTC by burning gtcbBTCc shares" and add an interpolatedIntent "Withdraw {assets} to {receiver}".

cases.notes: The 130000 sats of cbBTC in match 'Withdraw exactly 0.0013 cbBTC'. The shares burned (1290996558190803) are not shown, and the reader inferred the direction but not the amount or the ticker.

formats.key: redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address owner)
effects: The vault burns exactly `shares` gtcbBTCc from `owner`. When the caller is not `owner`, the call spends the owner's share allowance to the caller.
The vault sends cbBTC to `receiver`. It computes the amount from the share price, rounding down, and the call sets no minimum.
formats.shown: Intent 'Redeem', the gtcbBTCc shares redeemed, the recipient and the owner. Nothing names the asset received.

findings.title: redeem never names cbBTC as the asset the receiver gets; the mint format shows it with a constant.
findings.evidence: descriptor redeem format: the fields are only 'Shares to redeem', 'To', 'Owner'. ERC4626._withdraw: `SafeERC20.safeTransfer(_asset, receiver, assets);`. Case 3: the signer receives 110050 sats of cbBTC, and the reader wrote 'Which token I get back (name suggests cbBTC but screen doesn't say)'.
findings.fix: Add a field {"label": "Receive asset", "format": "raw", "value": "$.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker"} and change the intent to "Redeem gtcbBTCc shares for cbBTC".

findings.title: redeem shows no amount or minimum of cbBTC received, because the vault computes it from storage.
findings.evidence: MetaMorpho.redeem: `assets = _convertToAssetsWithTotals(shares, totalSupply(), newTotalAssets, Math.Rounding.Floor);` The call has no minimum-out parameter. Case 3: 110050 sats of cbBTC in, with no amount on screen.

cases.notes: The shares out match the screen exactly. For the cbBTC in, the screen gives neither the asset nor the amount; the reader guessed cbBTC.
